signature.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
signature.detail: This is the memorial and mausoleum of Ghana's first president, Kwame Nkrumah, and the most visited sight in Accra. It combines a museum, gardens and the tomb itself, so it gives a first-time visitor the country's modern history in one stop. Go in the morning to avoid the midday heat, and bring small cash for the modest entry fee.

signature.name: Independence Square, Accra
signature.detail: This vast ceremonial square on the coast is where Ghana marks its independence, with the Black Star Gate and memorial arches as its icons. It is free to walk around and best visited early morning or late afternoon for cooler air and better light. It sits close to Osu, so you can combine it with a walk through that district.

signature.name: Osu Castle
signature.detail: A centuries-old coastal fort that served as seat of government for much of Ghana's history, it is a key stop for understanding the city's colonial and post-independence past. Access is often restricted because it remains a state building, so check opening arrangements before you go rather than assuming you can walk in. It is a short drive from Independence Square.

signature.name: Makola Market
signature.detail: Accra's biggest and busiest market is a full sensory experience of food, fabric and everyday commerce, and it is a must for seeing the city at work. Go early in the morning when it is cooler and less crowded, and keep valuables close in the narrow lanes. It is central and easy to reach by taxi or trotro.

signature.name: Jamestown Lighthouse
signature.detail: The lighthouse stands over the old Jamestown harbour, one of the city's oldest quarters, with good views over the fishing community and coastline. Come in the late afternoon for softer light and a walk around the nearby streets. It is west of the centre and best reached by taxi.

transport: Trotro ride under $1; taxi or ride-hailing trip $3-8
